title: Speaker G S Patil summons Forest officials over elephant relocation row - Deccan Herald
content: Speaker of the Legislative Assembly G S Patil has summoned officials of the Forest Department for a meeting on Wednesday to discuss the relocation of elephants from Belur in Hassan district to the Bhadra Tiger Reserve Chikkamagaluru after legislators from the latter district threatened to resign over the development. Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office on Monday in a sign of protest. However, she did accompany Chikkamagaluru MLA H D Thammaiah and Tarikere MLA G H Srinivas to the meeting with Patil, who was apprised of the situation. Motamma said that the Speaker was convening a meeting of the Forest Department officials and four MLAs, including Sringeri MLA T D Rajegowda, whose constituency will also be impacted by the relocation operation. "The Speaker was surprised to learn that the foresters had undertaken the operation without taking the legislators, planters' association and farmers into confidence," Motamma said. Accusing the Forest Department of entirely disregarding the safety of the people of Chikkamagaluru, Motamma asked, "Who will be held responsible for any loss of life during the operation? What is the guarantee these relocated elephants will not stray into human habitats later." Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, who is currently touring Japan, is learnt to have spoken to the Chikkamagaluru legislators, and asked them to keep their resignation in abeyance, while promising them that the issue would be resolved. "The CM has instructed the Forest Department to put the operation on hold till he returns to Bengaluru on Wednesday night," said Motamma. Disputing the foresters' claims that the elephants had moved to the Bhadra Tiger Reserve of their own accord, Motamma said, "They were driven there to ease the pressure on the forest in Hassan. But our district is already grappling with human-animal conflict given that there are around 400 elephants in the region." Meanwhile, KPCC president B K Hariprasad urged Nayana Motamma to reconsider her decision to resign, saying the issue would be resolved through discussions with the government. He said the MLA had agreed to hold back her resignation for now and that a decision would be taken after the chief minister returns from Japan.

title: Choi Ga-eun Ties Career High in GS Caltex Victory - 조선일보
content: Middle blocker's 15 points and '50% mindset' lead team to first-round finish [Daejeon = Sports Chosun Reporter Lee Jong-seo] "When I think I need to do well, I end up performing worse." Choi Ga-eun, 25 years old (GS Caltex), tied her personal best score with 15 points in the first-round match against Jung Kwan Jang Red Sparrows in the HK Insurance 2026-2027 V-League women's division, held at Chungmu Gymnasium in Daejeon on November 24. She also recorded a personal best of 4 points from serves and 5 blocks. GS Caltex, led by Choi Ga-eun's performance, defeated Jung Kwan Jang with a set score of 3-1 and finished the first round in first place. After the match, Choi Ga-eun said, "It was the last game of the first round, and I’m glad we could finish in first place. There were difficult moments, but it was good that the players overcame them." This season has started well. In 3 out of 6 games in the first round, she scored double-digit points, and she consistently recorded blocks in every game. She has firmly established herself as the team’s starting middle blocker. Lee Young-taek, GS Caltex’s head coach, also smiles and says, "She is doing well," but adds a word of caution: "While I give appropriate praise, getting too excited when things go well can have a negative effect." Choi Ga-eun, along with Kwon Min-ji, is a 'mood maker' for GS Caltex. Her bright energy injects vitality into the team, but there’s a concern that if she gets too excited, she might become unstable. The coach said, "I lightly point out things when needed to help her manage her mind. (Choi) Ga-eun has bright energy, but sometimes she rushes too much. I talk to her about those aspects." Choi Ga-eun seemed aware of the coach’s intentions. Regarding the coach’s advice, she laughed and said, "He gives me more whips than carrots," adding, "It has a good influence in filling my shortcomings." She also has her own unique 'mantra': "Do 50%." She explained, "If I get greedy and try too hard, it doesn’t work. When things don’t go well, self-blame grows bigger. So I enter the game comfortably, thinking, ‘Just do 50% of what I prepared.’ My performance comes out well, and even when things don’t go smoothly, I can let it go." She added, "In games where my condition is bad or I feel pressured, if I think, ‘I must do well,’ I can’t perform. I focus on helping and being helped well." The personal best-tying 15 points on November 24 were also born from the coach’s advice. Choi Ga-eun said, "With the team’s good performance and my own form, I had a desire for more points, but yesterday after training, the coach said, ‘If you sacrifice and help instead of being greedy for points, things will go well.’ I didn’t push for points and blended into the team, which led to scoring well." Her personal best of 4 serve points that day also came after letting go of greed. Choi Ga-eun said, "During the season preparation, we emphasized managing unforced errors. As a middle blocker, if I serve and make an error, I get replaced by the libero and lose the chance to recover. Instead of aiming for points, I focused on placing the serve where I intended, which led to positive results." Mindset isn’t everything. All of this was possible due to intense training. Choi Ga-eun recalled the off-season, saying, "The secret to this year’s performance is the high training volume. Even though we were champions, our vacation wasn’t long. Returning early and syncing with the players was the key."

title: Seoul Redevelopment Projects Awarded Without Competition - 조선일보
content: As overseas markets decline, firms focus domestically, sparking concerns over non-competitive bidding practices DL E&C and GS Engineering & Construction each secured redevelopment and reconstruction projects worth trillions of Korean won in Seoul on November 21–22. DL E&C won the construction rights for the Seongsu Strategic Maintenance Zone District 2 redevelopment project in Seongdong-gu, valued at 2.0137 trillion Korean won, while GS Engineering & Construction secured the Mokdong New Town 12th Complex reconstruction project in Yangcheon-gu, worth 1.7887 trillion Korean won. Both Seongsu and Mokdong, core residential areas in Seoul, were considered lucrative projects offering both profitability and symbolic value for construction firms. Both companies secured their respective projects without competition, as no rivals participated in the bidding process, leading to direct negotiations with the associations. A notable trend in domestic maintenance projects this year has been the disappearance of competition. Earlier in the year, intense competition was expected for high-profit projects like the so-called ‘Apyeongyeomokseong’ (Apgujeong, Yeouido, Mokdong, and Seongsu). However, most projects ended up being awarded without competition. Concerns have arisen that the lack of competition could limit the associations’ options. Domestic maintenance projects have been booming at record levels in recent years. According to industry sources on the 24th, the top 10 construction companies by construction capability had already secured 50.4 trillion Korean won in maintenance projects by the 13th of this year, surpassing last year’s record annual total of 48.6 trillion Korean won. Hyundai Engineering & Construction (13 trillion Korean won) and Samsung C&T (12 trillion Korean won) led the pack, with GS Engineering & Construction also exceeding 7 trillion Korean won in orders. However, the market has seen a trend of dividing projects rather than fierce competition. For instance, only Hyundai Engineering & Construction participated in the bidding for the Mokdong New Town 4th Complex reconstruction project, which closed on the 16th. Despite its scale of 1.6389 trillion Korean won, it received a sole bid. If fewer than two companies participate in a competitive bid for a maintenance project, it is deemed unsuccessful, and if it fails twice, it proceeds to direct negotiation. Among the six Mokdong complexes where construction companies have been selected or are being finalized, Hyundai Engineering & Construction (4th and 10th complexes), DL E&C (6th complex), Daewoo Engineering & Construction (8th complex), GS Engineering & Construction (12th complex), and Samsung C&T (13th complex) each secured or bid alone. Industry insiders attribute the lack of competition to the prolonged boom in large-scale maintenance projects in Seoul’s core areas. With abundant projects, companies tend to avoid overlapping bids. A source from a major construction firm explained, “Large-scale projects like the Apgujeong 3rd District, which exceeds 5 trillion Korean won, require a deposit of 200 billion Korean won alone during bidding, making it impractical to participate in multiple large projects simultaneously.” He added, “There’s intense strategic maneuvering to reduce sunk costs.” Some suspect collusion among companies. The Korea Fair Trade Commission’s establishment of a Construction Energy Cartel Investigation Division last month reflects this concern. It is unusual for a dedicated team to focus on such cases. The commission began investigating six construction companies on the 28th of last month over alleged bid-rigging in projects commissioned by the Korea Land & Housing Corporation (LH) and is also examining potential collusion in private maintenance projects. However, selective bidding—where major firms target only projects they are certain to win—is expected to continue. While overseas construction markets are struggling, domestic maintenance projects remain steady. According to the International Contractors Association of Korea, the top 10 construction companies’ overseas orders from January to October this year amounted to 9.1619 billion dollars, a 35.6% decrease from the same period last year. Lee Eun-hyeong, a researcher at the Korea Research Institute for Construction Policy, warned, “If non-competitive bidding persists domestically, associations may face difficulties comparing conditions from multiple contractors, leading to unintended consequences.”

title: GS Caltex Seoul KIXX Tops First Round With Four-Game Streak - 조선일보
content: Coach Lee's strategic moves, including captain Yu Seo-yeon's third-set entry, and key players' performances secure victory [Daejeon = Sports Chosun Lee Jong-seo] GS Caltex Seoul KIXX advanced through the first round in first place. GS Caltex defeated Jung Kwan Jang Redsparks of the HK Savings Bank 2026–2027 V-League women’s division 3–1 (25–21, 28–30, 25–16, 25–13) in a first-round match held at Chungmu Gymnasium in Daejeon on the 24th. GS Caltex recorded 5 wins, 1 loss, and 15 points with a four-game winning streak, taking first place ahead of Korea Expressway Corporation Hi-Pass (5 wins, 1 loss, 15 points, set ratio 2.500) in set ratio. Before the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, “Reducing our reliance on Silva, who has always been a constant for us, worked well. Our blocking wasn’t great, so we focused heavily on serves. The serves went in well, which helped the blocking. The momentum from winning the Cup tournament carried over, which was fortunate, even though we prepared during the off-season.” The positive atmosphere continued. GS Caltex was led by Silva (22 points), Tanacha (19 points), and Choi Ga-eun (15 points), who all scored in double digits. Although they had regrets after losing the second set in a deuce, they prevented the momentum from shifting in the third set and successfully secured all three set points. After the match, Coach Lee said, “Overall, we handled things well. The opponent’s serves were strong, but we held our ground. If we had lost the second set after going to deuce, the momentum could have shifted, but the players maintained good focus in the third set and turned things around.” Despite losing the second set, Coach Lee focused on encouraging the players rather than showing impatience. He said, “We lost the second set narrowly, but I told them their performance wasn’t bad. There were one or two critical moments, and since it was an away game with young players, they looked flustered, so I urged them to stay calm. I told them to stay positive because their performance was coming together.” The decision to start captain Yu Seo-yeon from the third set, who wasn’t in the starting lineup for the first and second sets, proved effective. Coach Lee said, “When Seo-yeon enters the game, the team stabilizes in terms of attack, defense, and connections. As the captain, she leads well when the momentum is swinging. I put her in with that in mind.” Choi Ga-eun’s performance, who tied her personal best with 15 points, brought a satisfied smile. Coach Lee said, “She’s doing well. I praise her appropriately, but when things go well, getting overexcited can backfire. I give her light feedback to help her manage her emotions. She has bright energy, but sometimes she rushes. I talk to her about that.” GS Caltex, which finished the first round in first place, will begin the second round against Hongkuk Life on the 27th at Incheon Samsan Gymnasium.

title: GS Caltex Seoul KIXX Tops First Round With Four Straight Wins - 조선일보
content: Defeats Jung Kwan Jang Red Sparks 3-0, securing 5 wins, 1 loss, 15 points in V-League Women's Division [Daejeon = Sports Chosun Lee Jong-seo Reporter] GS Caltex Seoul KIXX finished the first round in first place with a four-game winning streak. GS Caltex defeated Jung Kwan Jang Red Sparks in the first-round match of the HK Financial Group 2026-2027 V-League Women’s Division held at Chungmu Gymnasium in Daejeon on the 24th with a set score of 3-0 (25-21, 28-30, 25-16, 25-13). GS Caltex recorded a four-game winning streak, finishing with 5 wins, 1 loss, and 15 points. At the same time, they rose to first place ahead of Korea Expressway Corporation Hi-Pass (5 wins, 1 loss, 15 points, set ratio 2.500) in set ratio. Jung Kwan Jang, ranked fourth, halted their two-game winning streak and fell to 3 wins, 3 losses, and 8 points. Both teams were on an upward trend with consecutive wins. Before the match, GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, “The atmosphere is still good. The players are preparing well in a positive mood.” Jung Kwan Jang head coach Kwon Soon-chan also emphasized composure, saying, “The atmosphere remains the same.” However, Jung Kwan Jang’s foreign player Bukirich has been sidelined since the Cup tournament due to a thigh injury. Coach Kwon said, “Bukirich has started ball exercises. He won’t play today,” explaining his condition. GS Caltex crushed Jung Kwan Jang with Silva (22 points), Tanacha (19 points), and Choi Ga-eun (15 points) each scoring double digits. Jung Kwan Jang’s Park Yeoreum (18 points) and Jong Hwi (15 points) fought hard but failed to prevent the defeat. GS Caltex took the first set. Silva was the decisive scorer. With an attack share rate of 35.90%—similar to Kwon Min-ji (30.77%) and Tanacha (25.64%)—Silva recorded an attack success rate of 57.14% and scored 8 points. Kwon Min-ji and Tanacha each added 4 points to the attack. Middle blocker Choi Ga-eun also contributed 3 points, including 2 blocking points, disrupting Jung Kwan Jang’s flow. GS Caltex easily secured the first set 25-21. In the second set, Park Yeoreum of Jung Kwan Jang exploded. With an attack success rate of 53.33% and 10 points, she bombarded GS Caltex’s court. Even in a tense deuce situation, Park Yeoreum maintained focus. She secured consecutive attack points from 28-28 to claim the second-set victory. Stunned, GS Caltex regrouped. In the third set, Choi Ga-eun’s quick attack was followed by Tanacha’s ace serve. With GS Caltex leading 16-13, Choi Ga-eun’s block and Kim Hyo-im’s serve point widened the gap. GS Caltex sealed the third set 24-16 with Oh Se-yeon’s block. The momentum carried into the fourth set. Early on, Tanacha’s open attacks and Choi Ga-eun’s quick attacks combined. Leading 11-5, Choi Ga-eun’s ace serve solidified the atmosphere. At 15-7, Silva’s open attack forced GS Caltex’s second technical timeout. GS Caltex continued to extend their lead and successfully secured 3 winning points.

title: Japanese Stocks Are Projected to Rally Again in the Coming Year - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The Japanese stock market’s gains this year have been driven largely by the banking and artificial intelligence (AI) sectors. Goldman Sachs Research expects the performance to broaden going forward, particularly because of the government’s push for corporations to use their cash to invest in growth. As long as capital expenditures in AI are ongoing, Japanese equity earnings per share (EPS) are forecast to increase again in fiscal year 2027—though at a more modest pace, Bruce Kirk, chief Japan equity strategist, writes in a report. Goldman Sachs Research projects the TOPIX of Japanese equities to rally about 20% to 4,500 in the next 12 months (as of November 24), based on estimates for growth in EPS of 9% in fiscal year 2027. “We believe that 2027 will be a transitional year for the Japanese equities market,” Kirk writes. The main drivers of Japanese stock gains for the past three years have been AI and normalization by the Bank of Japan. In 2027, Kirk expects investors’ tactical diversification into less crowded positions and less volatile themes, combined with the government’s market-wide efforts for corporations to invest sensibly in future growth, to produce a shift in the factors propelling the market. Communications from Japan’s Tokyo Stock Exchange; the Financial Services Agency; the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry; and the Takaichi administration suggest “a well-coordinated shift in top-down pressure towards promoting the use of excess cash reserves to drive the future growth initiatives across corporate Japan,” Kirk writes. “Growth” is the key word in Japan's corporate governance reforms, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “This should lead to a re-focus of interest on corporate governance-related themes in 2027, but skewed more towards growth investment and corporate restructuring,” Kirk writes. Our strategists have argued that improvement in return-on-equity at the index level will require “more drastic corporate structuring measures” than have taken place so far. These measures include mergers and acquisitions, operating segment restructuring, and consolidation. “This is where we think investor interest will shift towards in 2027,” Kirk writes. Goldman Sachs Research notes that, despite recent improvements, the TOPIX's return on equity still lags behind a wide range of markets globally. One of the best ways to address this gap would be to promote sector consolidation via increased levels of domestic mergers and acquisitions, Kirk writes. Prime Minister Takaichi's growth strategy highlights 17 strategic sectors and 62 key products and technologies. The strategy is designed to promote investments that enhance resilience against potential crises and promote growth, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “Without secure and reliable access to energy, power generation, natural resources, critical minerals, and rare earths, most of the other growth strategies will become almost impossible to achieve,” Kirk writes. As part of a $550 billion trade deal between the US and Japan, a number of power generation and energy security-related projects have already been approved or announced. “We see significant overlap between the Japanese government's energy and resource-related initiatives and future partnership opportunities with the US administration,” Kirk writes. Kirk identifies five key themes for investors in Japanese equities in 2027: AI innovation and quality: Goldman Sachs Research’s framework for AI-related stocks sorts them into two core groups: the AI semiconductor ecosystem and the AI data center hardware ecosystem. While the correlation between the two groups is “extremely high,” Kirk points out that AI companies in this dataset that scored highly in terms of innovation and quality significantly outperformed those that scored lower between April 2025 and June 2026. Corporate restructuring: Japan's new corporate governance code focuses on "growth-oriented governance." It urges corporate investment that supports sustainable mid- to long-term growth. It also stresses fair treatment of minority shareholders during mergers. Goldman Sachs Research expects a significant rise in takeover bids, management buyouts, and industry consolidation from 2027 onward. Physical AI: Labor costs for non-financial TOPIX companies reached 10.5% of sales in fiscal year 2025, up from 8.5% in fiscal year 2016. This is the highest level in a decade, excluding distortions during Covid. Goldman Sachs Research analysts forecast that humanoid robot prices, meanwhile, will decline from about $42,000 in 2025 to $21,000 by 2035. The government’s strategy aims for the deployment of 350,000 AI robots by 2030 and about 10 million by 2040. Energy and resource security: Japan imports almost all of its oil, natural gas, coal, and critical minerals. Its energy self-sufficiency fell from 22% in fiscal year 1998 to 6% after the shutdown of the Fukushima nuclear power station in 2011. While that figure recovered to 16% by 2024, Japan remains highly vulnerable to supply disruptions. The government's growth strategy aims to diversify sources of minerals and raw materials; secure energy supplies; strengthen the production supply chain for components; and expand solar, thermal, and advanced nuclear power. These plans could benefit trading companies, shipping firms, energy companies, and heavy industry. Cybersecurity: Japan's growth strategy explicitly prioritizes security products and services suited to the AI era, including support for domestic technology development and adoption. The government aims for domestic cybersecurity companies to generate annual revenue of more than 3 trillion yen ($18.8 billion) by 2035. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. European stocks are forecast to rise in 2027, but to post lower returns than their counterparts in the US and Asia, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Slower earnings growth, weaker economic growth, and high public deficits and energy prices are expected to weigh on European stocks, writes Sharon Bell, senior European equity strategist for Goldman Sachs Research. “That said, European equities continue to deliver positive performance, offer several attractive characteristics to global investors, and we expect continued positive flows especially from foreign investors,” Bell adds. Our strategists forecast a 9% total return for Europe’s STOXX 600 index over the next 12 months (as of November 13). European equity returns have historically tracked earnings growth expectations, and current estimates of growth in European earnings per share (EPS) are “consistent with positive but low returns” for stocks, Bell observes. That said, equity performance has already slowed significantly relative to earnings growth, she adds—the STOXX 600 is up around 10% in 2026 (as of November 23), even as company earnings are substantially higher than that. Next year, earnings growth is expected to slow to 7%, from 18% this year. “The slowdown is partly a function of Energy EPS decline and partly a function of weaker economic growth and margins next year as we see the impact of higher energy costs and rates feed through,” Bell writes. European stocks trade at a discount to their US counterparts, but that discount has narrowed substantially since late 2024. The discount as a proportion of stocks’ price/earnings ratios is now at 14% on a sector-adjusted basis, having once been as large as 34%. Since 2022, Germany’s DAX index and the UK’s FTSE 100 index have kept pace with the S&P 500 in terms of total returns, partly as a function of European stocks narrowing their valuation discount against US peers. “Accordingly, we think that European indexes are likely to lag modestly over the next year given the valuation gap to the US is now smaller, and roughly in line with its history, and given that earnings growth is likely to be slower in Europe than in other regions,” Bell writes. Our strategists anticipate positive flows into European stocks next year, especially from foreign investors. Bell identifies several reasons why she expects global investors to continue allocating capital to the region: AI-diversification benefits: On average, European indexes—especially Switzerland’s SMI and the UK’s FTSE 100—have been resilient (and even risen) as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks decline. Relatively high free cash flow: High cash spending has eroded free cash flow for US companies, which also limits their ability to buy back their shares. This has happened at the same time as more IPOs and expiring lock-ups are increasing the net supply of stocks to the market, which can weigh on stock valuations. In contrast, free cash flow for European stocks remains relatively high, and buybacks remain strong. At the same time, M&A activity is robust, and a smaller volume of new stocks is coming to the market via IPOs in Europe. “In other words, shrinking net equity supply continues to support Europe regardless of investor allocations,” Bell explains. Keen international investors: Goldman Sachs Research already sees evidence of flows into European stocks from outside the continent. “We find global investors, especially from the US, are allocating increasing amounts to Europe, mainly via global and global ex-US funds, while domestic European investors still appear reluctant to allocate,” Bell writes. Energy prices will be key for European stocks in 2027. “European equities have the most to gain from relief on energy supply and prices (and, of course, the most to lose if this does not happen),” Bell writes. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that each 10% rise in the price of Brent crude oil takes around 1% off the valuations of European stocks. Our commodities strategists expect both Brent crude and European liquefied natural gas to decline in 2027 as suppliers adapt to disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil is forecast to fall to $78 per barrel by the end of 2027 from around $91.50 today (as of November 23). Some European sectors tend to perform better when energy prices fall. Cyclical stocks, German blue-chip companies in the DAX index, and consumer discretionary stocks would stand to benefit the most as gas prices decline, while energy, quality stocks, defensives, and the UK’s FTSE 100 index are all likely to be underperformers. “All other things being equal, lower energy prices through 2027 militate against shifting more towards quality or defensives in our allocation and push toward more cyclical exposure despite a likely window for weaker economic growth in Europe over the winter,” Bell writes. European corporate balance sheets are not stretched—Europe’s technology companies have exceptionally low debt—and stock valuations held up comparatively well when European government bond yields rose compared with their peers this year. At the same time, “it is difficult to argue that Europe equities can disentangle themselves from a broader sovereign risk event, especially banks and other domestic stocks,” Bell writes. While our economists do not forecast a sovereign risk event for 2027, the indebtedness of European governments undoubtedly remains a drag on growth, she adds. Historically, a 10-basis-point widening in the OAT-Bund spread, the premium that investors require for holding a French government bond rather than a comparable German government bond, has been associated with a decline of around 3% for France’s CAC 40 index of large-cap stocks and a decline of 4% for French domestic stocks. “We think it is too early to re-engage with French domestic stocks,” Bell writes. Her team prefers getting exposure to Germany and the DAX index, given relatively low valuations and continued fiscal spending by the German government, or to UK domestic stocks, which could benefit if UK government bond yields and energy prices fall next year. title: Exclusive: TSSA council calls for suspension of no-confidenced GS - skwawkbox
content: News, politics, insights, inside information from the left A major body of the TSSA rail union has voted no confidence in the union’s general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust – and called for her immediate suspension pending full investigation into her conduct, the resulting damage to the union’s democracy and integrity and the paralysis of the union’s ruling executive. The London South Divisional Council has acted on correspondence it received from executive (EC) members across the country: The London South Divisional Council notes the following correspondence from four TSSA EC members: Update to TSSA Members from Executive Committee Members We are writing to update you on the current situation within the TSSA Executive Committee (EC). The EC is currently unable to function effectively. Meetings are not being convened, important business remains outstanding, and decisions requiring the EC’s collective consideration are being delayed. This situation is preventing us, as elected EC members, from fully exercising our responsibilities under the TSSA Rule Book and providing the oversight and accountability that members rightly expect. We have raised these concerns internally and sought to resolve them, but the situation remains unchanged. The continued paralysis of the EC is unacceptable. The democratically elected governing body of our union must be able to meet, conduct its business and make decisions in the interests of members. We remain fully committed to our elected roles and will continue working to restore the effective functioning of the EC. We believe members have a right to know about these difficulties and will provide further updates as matters develop. The undersigned members of the TSSA Executive Committee In response, the council has declared its ‘no confidence’ in Eslamdoust – who was appointed despite a lack of relevant experience, with the support of allies of disgraced former general secretary Manuel Cortes. It also condemns the union leadership’s evasion demands immediate action from the EC: suspend Eslamdoust pending a formal and independent investigation and protect union members and staff, and EC members themselves, from attacks for whistleblowing: This Divisional Council concludes that the continuing failure to respond to the concerns formally raised by members and branches, together with the matters outlined above, demonstrates a serious and continuing breakdown in democratic accountability and confidence in the present leadership. The DC further concludes that there can be no credible return to normal democratic trade union governance while these matters remain unresolved and while the present leadership arrangements continue unchanged. This Divisional council therefore calls upon the Executive Committee to: This Divisional council has no confidence in the General Secretary and calls upon the Executive Committee to act immediately to restore confidence in the democratic governance, accountability and integrity of the Association. Union staff have been in dispute with Maryam Eslamdoust for almost three years, including repeated strike action, over complaints of bullying, victimisation and harassment. Eslamdoust has also repeatedly and publicly attacked the GMB union that represents TSSA staff in their workplace, including twice in the national media. She has suspended a number of GMB reps as part of what staff say are anti-union manoeuvres aimed at breaking their industrial action – and ultimately she and her allies on the EC de-recognised the union. Her allies on the union’s executive expelled TSSA’s retired assistant general secretary for whistle-blowing about abuse and anti-democratic manoeuvres. Eslamdoust has been the subject of repeated, heavily-supported no-confidence motions, and wrecked the union’s conference to prevent another. She and her team have twice annulled elections in which members had voted her rivals into the key positions of treasurer and president. And on the same day as the new unanimous vote against her, TSSA declared her ally as the new, uncontested treasurer after again suspending the candidate who beat her. Retired assistant general secretary Steve Coe is suing Eslamdoust for defaming him after he criticised her conduct and manoeuvres to try to keep cronies in elected positions, and is taking TSSA to the union regulator for its treatment of him. title: This Acura Integra GS-R For Sale Is The 2 Fast 2 Furious Car Of Your Dreams - CarScoops
content: It's supercharged, dripping in red, and selling with no reserve. The Nissan Skyline, Mazda RX-7, and Toyota Supra were far from the only beloved Japanese sports cars used throughout the Fast and Furious franchise. During the first film, two Acura Integras were used, including one driven by Mia Toretto, played by Jordana Brewster. As it turns out, an Integra GS-R also served as an extra in "2 Fast 2 Furious" and is now up for auction in the U.S. The Bring a Trailer auction doesn't note if the car had any screen time, but documents from filming in 2002 show the production company behind the film was charged $2,472 for damage to the Integra's front and rear bumpers and grille. The year after serving as an extra, the car was repainted in a combination of black and red. This Integra certainly isn't as cool as Brian O'Conner's Nissan R34 Skyline GT-R, but it will be a lot more affordable, so it has that going for it. Contrasting the exterior paint is a set of 10-spoke 19-inch HRE wheels clad in 255/40 Firestone Firehawk tires. The Acura also includes a set of upgraded drilled-and-slotted brake discs and SSBC Force 10 calipers. It's under the hood where even more significant upgrades have been made. The original 1.8-liter inline-4 now includes a Jackson Racing supercharger and an aftermarket air intake. The listing doesn't make any mention of how much power the car has, though it's safe to assume it should be pretty sprightly. Drive is sent to the front wheels through a five-speed manual transmission. The engine bay also looks the part of a dramatic show car. It includes bright red hoses throughout, several chrome accents, and a red Comptech Sport strut bar. The wild red theme continues into the cabin, where the seats are trimmed in red and black, and there are red floor mats, a red instrument cluster, and red on the Momo steering wheel. There are also several carbon fiber accents inside, as well as an aftermarket audio system. An Integra like this is obviously an acquired taste and won't appeal to everyone. But for anyone who grew up wanting a "2 Fast 2 Furious" build, it ticks almost every box, and it's being offered with no reserve, so it might end up going for cheap. This generation of Integra, which spawned a Type R that sold for $204,000, is also well regarded for its handling, so while the exterior and interior are a little bold, it should be plenty of fun to drive.

title: Yeoju Farm Produce to Fill Lunch Trays at Seoul's GS Tower - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
'Yeoju Day' Set for Dec. 2 With Special Lunch Menus
Rice, Sweet Potatoes, Eggplant and Pears on the Menu YEOJU — The Yeoju Agricultural Industry Joint Brand Promotion Center said on the 24th that it will hold "Yeoju Day," a special lunch event featuring farm produce from Yeoju, at the GS Tower staff cafeteria in Seoul's Gangnam district on Dec. 2. The event is the second collaboration program with GS Group, following the "Yeoju Hansang" event held for group employees in July this year. The center plans to use Yeoju-grown produce — including Daewangnimpyo ("King's Mark") Yeoju rice, the city's premium rice brand, as well as sweet potatoes, eggplant and pears — to introduce cafeteria diners to the taste and quality of the region's farm goods. The menus will be offered at three stations in the GS Tower cafeteria: Great G 700, Great R and Great E. The Great G 700 station will serve a "Yeoju set meal" built around rice and sweet potato nutritious rice. It comes with handmade tteokgalbi topped with peanuts, spicy pork belly gochujang stew, stir-fried eggplant, fresh pear and water parsley salad, and lightly seasoned cabbage kimchi. The Great R station will feature vegetable and shrimp tendon (tempura rice bowl) made with Yeoju produce as its main dish, served with mini warm buckwheat noodles, honey butter whole sweet potato, Yeoju pear and arugula salad, and a soft-boiled egg. At the Great E station, diners can choose from pork belly steak with sweet pumpkin puree, Mexican beef rice, eggplant caponata, honey butter sweet potato, parmesan-crusted mushroom, dolce corn soup and mandarin pomegranate salad. All three stations will serve Pascucci's "Yeoju rice gelato" for dessert. The product was developed through a cooperative partnership between the city of Yeoju and Pascucci, and is currently sold at about 500 Pascucci stores nationwide. It lets customers enjoy the nutty flavor characteristic of Yeoju rice as a dessert. The center said the event matters because it goes beyond simple promotion, letting people experience Yeoju produce in an actual consumption setting. The aim is to use the corporate cafeteria — an everyday dining space — to broaden the potential uses of Daewangnimpyo Yeoju rice and other local farm products. "The response from GS Group employees at the last event was good, so we are introducing Yeoju produce again," center head Lee Sang-hwi said. "The surest form of promotion is for consumers to taste it themselves and feel the difference." Lee added, "Through this Yeoju Day, we hope the taste of Daewangnimpyo Yeoju rice and the appeal of Yeoju farm products become more widely known." title: Starting Chess at 39 to Winning 3 Asian Medals for India: Ezhilarasi G’s Journey - ChessBase India
content: For most competitive players, turning 39 marks a step back from the tournaments, but for Bengaluru-based Ezhilarasi G., it was the beginning of an extraordinary journey. Affected by polio at the age of three, she discovered structured chess during the COVID-19 lockdown and, within four years, represented India at the 4th Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities in Bishkek, winning one silver and two bronze medals. In her own words, she shares how determination and support turned a childhood pastime into an international podium finish. My name is Ezhilarasi. I am 43 years old, originally from Nathamalai village in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, and currently residing in Bengaluru, Karnataka. I was affected by polio at the age of three, resulting in a physical disability affecting both my legs. Due to my circumstances, I had to discontinue my formal education after Class 8. Growing up in a small village, I had very limited exposure to the outside world. From the age of 14 until around 30, I spent most of my time at home. During my childhood, as I was not attending school, I started playing chess at home with my brother. At that time, I had no idea that chess could offer opportunities beyond simply playing a game. Gradually, I developed a special interest in it, little knowing that it would one day become such an important part of my life. Later, due to personal and family circumstances, I left home and started working with NGOs. I learned embroidery, handicrafts and other creative skills, and eventually began teaching these skills to persons with disabilities. During my work with an NGO in Chennai, I met my husband, Adarsh Edamana, at the age of 31. We got married two years later, in 2016, and eventually settled in Bengaluru. My husband has always been my biggest strength, encouraging me to pursue my dreams and supporting me through every difficulty. My serious chess journey began at the age of 39 during the COVID-19 lockdown, when I started playing again at home. I decided to learn the game properly. Since travelling to a training centre was difficult, my first coach, Karthik, came to my home and trained me for around three months. Later, I met with an accident and suffered a fracture in my right hand, but I did not give up chess. I came to know about the Chess Federation for Physically Disabled (CFPD), which supports persons with disabilities through chess. In December 2022, I participated in my first national-level competition at Tumakuru. There, I met Mr Anand Babu VL, Secretary of CFPD, who encouraged and supported me in participating in tournaments and selection events. I also met Coach NI – Dinakaran B, who has been training and guiding me ever since. Their support has played an important role in my progress. In 2024, I participated in the Tata Steel 4th All India Specially Abled FIDE Rated Chess Championship, held in Jharkhand, and secured first place in the Unrated Category with 5.5 points. I qualified for the 2nd Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities 2024, held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. I scored 6 points out of 9 rounds and secured fourth place in the women's championship. After that, I participated in a few national and international tournaments but could not achieve the results I had hoped for. However, I continued participating, learning from every experience and working to improve my game. In May 2026, I participated in the Chief Minister Trophy – 6th CFPD National Chess Championship 2026, held in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, from 27 to 30 May 2026. I secured 2nd Position (Silver Medal) in the Wheelchair Women (WC-Women) category. This achievement paved the way for my selection by the Sports Authority of India (SAI) to represent India internationally. My biggest achievement came when I represented India at the 4th Asian Chess Championship for Players with Disabilities, held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, from 29 October to 8 November 2026. Being one of the nine players representing India was a proud moment. I was also the only woman representing Karnataka and the only woman above 40 years of age in the Indian contingent. I won three medals for India: Silver in Women's Rapid Chess and Bronze in Women's Blitz and Women's Standard (Classical) Chess. Standing on the international podium and representing my country was an unforgettable experience. I am deeply grateful to my husband, Adarsh Edamana, Mr Anand Babu VL, Secretary of CFPD, for his encouragement and support, Coach Dinakaran B for his continuous training and guidance, and Mr Tamil Arasan, our team manager, for supporting us and taking care of the arrangements throughout the championship. My journey has also involved financial difficulties. After COVID, my husband lost his job, making it challenging to manage household expenses and support my chess career. Due to financial constraints, I could not participate in as many tournaments as I wanted. Nevertheless, we have managed with whatever resources we have and continued supporting my chess journey. At present, I teach chess to a few children at home, helping them learn the game from the basics. This provides me with a livelihood while allowing me to share my knowledge and love for chess. Alongside teaching, I continue to train and prepare for upcoming competitions. My dream is to keep improving, participate in more international competitions and win gold medals for India. title: The Best Matzo Ball Soup In Los Angeles Might Be Better Than Bubbe's - Tasting Table
content: The original Birdie G's in Santa Monica opened in 2019, and it was quickly recognized as one of the best restaurants in Los Angeles for its Jewish-American-inspired menu. When it opened, The Los Angeles Times called it "Santa Monica's hottest restaurant of the year." Later, the restaurant was named a Michelin Bib Gourmand. One of the signature dishes that earned Birdie G's all its accolades is chef Jeremy Fox's comforting yet elegant matzo ball soup, which some say is the best in the region. There are three key ingredients for traditional matzo balls: matzo meal, fat, and eggs. It's a seemingly simple dish, so what makes this matzo ball soup so special? Tasting Table spoke with chef Jeremy Fox to find out. The original Birdie G's closed at the end of 2025, but the restaurant recently reopened in Century City, bringing its beloved matzo ball soup to Los Angeles. To this day, the matzo ball soup is the dish that causes Fox the most stress because "I'm never going to beat that person's grandmother's matzo ball soup ... So I really work hard to make sure that ... the matzo ball soup is where it should be." Chef Jeremy Fox's matzo ball soup is richer and has more umami flavors than most — and he shared a lot of his matzo ball tips and tricks that make it so. First, he uses matzo meal from The Matzo Project in Brooklyn, New York, mixed with his house-rendered schmaltz, made by rendering chicken fat and onions. He told Tasting Table that the matzo meal and schmaltz are mixed with organic eggs and "lots of fresh dill," plus a little bit of baking powder. Fox takes inspiration from his grandmother's matzo ball soup, although he admittedly makes it in a different style. "Her matzo balls were very very light. Definitely floaters and ours are more sinkers," said Fox. The chicken broth, however, is labeled on the menu as "Rachael's chicken broth." It's named after Fox's wife, Rachael Sheridan, and is made using chicken backs, feet, and wings. "So it has a good amount of gelatin," he explained. After a cooking and cooling process, the stock then gets steeped with gribenes and dill stems. Fox said that enriches the stock and gives it a roasted chicken quality. The big matzo ball is served with some fresh carrots and fresh dill, and then topped with carrot miso. The stock is then poured tableside, melting the miso into the broth. From the dense yet still pillowy matzo ball to the rich chicken broth, and the umami from the carrot miso, this soup is the ultimate bowl of comfort.

title: Global Institute Summit 2026 - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. 2026 has been a year in which competition reshaped global capital flows, accelerated investments in new technologies and industries, and changed how nations wield geopolitical power to advance objectives. War in the Middle East moved energy markets and, through them, inflation, rates, and the economics of global industries. Russia’s war in Ukraine surpassed the duration of World War I, with no clear end in sight. And in the United States, midterm election results, debates over AI, and a positive if uncertain economic landscape have shifted the macro outlook. The Goldman Sachs Global Institute convened its fourth annual Global Affairs Summit, bringing together 150 attendees, including current and former government officials, experts in the fields of science and technology, and leading figures from the business world. Together, the group took stock of a year in which geopolitics and technological innovation were major themes for executives, investors, and public-sector leaders alike, and outlined the major debates shaping markets heading into 2027. President of Global Affairs and Global Institute Co-Head Jared Cohen hosted Ambassador Mike Waltz, US Representative to the United Nations, for a geopolitical assessment spanning Iran, Ukraine, and China. Economic pressure emerged as a common theme, with clear effects and limits. On Ukraine, negotiations have made limited progress, though the ongoing human toll of the war remains staggering and the hardest questions remain unresolved. Across all three theaters, geographic and market chokepoints are redefining how states confront, compete, and cooperate with one another, from Hormuz, to the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea, to the Arctic. Anshul Sehgal, Global Co-Head of Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities, Goldman Sachs, and Jared Cohen examined how a regional war in the Middle East has become a global market variable. Participants explored and debated potential future scenarios and outcomes, and consequently, the markets’ pricing of potential escalation scenarios. The discussion outlined how investors trace new kinds of risk and separate the signal from the noise. The group also discussed how risks in a theater like the Middle East connect to challenges elsewhere, including in the Indo-Pacific, the world’s most dynamic and populous region and home to some of its most important trade routes and technologies. John Hess, Former Chairman and CEO, Hess Corporation, and Tyler Miller, Global Co-Head of Power, Utilities, and Infrastructure, Goldman Sachs, described how the energy market is facing a security, affordability, and transition trilemma amid a historic oil and gas market disruption and pressure to meet unprecedented demand for power generation and transmission. In oil markets, thin inventory buffers are magnifying the price impact of further disruptions, with more than 500 million barrels already drawn from global inventories since the Iran War began. In power, the constraint has shifted from fuel to the physical and regulatory machinery of building, with an estimated 100 GW of additional US peak supply needed by 2030 and rapidly accelerating demands for capital. Energy has long driven economic growth and human progress. George Lee, Co-Head, Goldman Sachs Global Institute, and Chase Lochmiller, Co-Founder and CEO, Crusoe, discussed the domestic politics and global competition of the AI buildout, with nearly 80 gigawatts of US data center projects under construction. Participants agreed on the need for a greater understanding of the technology’s benefits, as well as its tradeoffs, and on the growing importance of earning the public’s trust that the benefits of AI will be widely shared. This issue is top of mind for voters, with 44 of 47 ballot initiatives challenging data center successful in this round of midterm elections alone. title: I swapped my Apple Watch Ultra for a sub-$250 outdoor watch - here's what I gained (and lost) - ZDNET
content: Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget. Why you can trust ZDNET: ZDNET independently tests and researches products to bring you our best recommendations and advice. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. The GS Explorer S beats the Apple Watch SE 3 on battery, GPS and water resistance, but lacks Apple's polished user experience. Back in October 2017, I took off my Casio G-Shock for the last time, strapped on an Apple Watch Series 3, and haven’t looked back. I worked my way up through Apple’s lineup until the Ultra was released in 2022. Today, I’m wearing an Ultra 4. Also: I tested the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and these 4 upgrades matter most Given how attached I’ve become to the Apple Watch, it’s rare for me to even review any alternatives (I gave the Garmin Fenix 8 Pro a go, but it wasn’t for me), so I was surprised to find how much I liked the sub-$300 Mibro GS Explorer S Titanium, a watch from a lesser-known brand. I got to test the titanium version of the GS Explorer S, but note there’s a cheaper ceramic model that’s virtually identical except for three things — the material (titanium alloy vs. ceramic and fiber-reinforced polymer), mapping (only the titanium version has offline mapping), and of course, price. The weight is also slightly different at 0.18 oz, but that’s small enough to ignore. To keep things simple, I’m not including the titanium version with the metal band in this comparison. Another feature that’s key to the success of a smartwatch is battery life. A few things stand out to me with this watch, both positive and negative. As an Apple Watch wearer, getting a couple of days from my Ultra is good, so I find going well over a week between charges quite remarkable. It eliminates that nightly charge, which I’d appreciate on those multi-day hikes where I’d normally take my Apple Watch charger. Also: Suunto Race 3S review: How real-time dynamic pacing improved my trail runs However, I’m so used to charging my Apple Watch nightly that it’s become a ritual, and switching to a weekly (or even less frequent) charging schedule makes it more likely I’ll forget. Also, it comes with a proprietary magnetic charging cable rather than a standard USB-C, which is a little more limiting. I suppose the good news is that if I lose it, there are replacements available. I like that it comes with two bands, which gives more options. I’m a fan of orange, so that’s my choice there. And, in contrast to a lot of smartwatches, changing the band is relatively easy because it uses a custom quick-release spring bar that can be opened with a finger. Nice touch. The Corning Gorilla Glass 3 gets a thumbs-up from me, despite being over a decade old. There are much worse materials to make a smartwatch crystal from, and I expect it to resist scratches, scrapes, and bumps well. For a rugged watch, the screen is the part most likely to get scratched, and decent protection is vital if the watch is to survive for any length of time. However, it’s not invulnerable by any stretch of the imagination. And I know from experience that it won’t be anywhere near as durable as the sapphire that’s on my Apple Watch Ultra. But that’s in a totally different price category. Another thumbs-up from me is the display’s 1,500-nit brightness, making it ideal for outdoor conditions. If you’re thinking of going for the titanium model to get your hands on mapping, know that the maps are limited to 31 x 31-mile (50 x 50 km) tiles, which explains the odd number. Also, while you get features such as route following, deviation alerts, one-tap return, and track-back navigation, it lacks advanced routing features like route creation and rerouting. Also: I tried a $200 smartwatch with voice recording – it beat the Apple Watch in a few key ways The mapping is also somewhat sparse. But remember, I’m from the UK and we have excellent Ordnance Survey mapping of the entire country down to 1:25,000 resolution at an incredible level of detail. So for me, anything that doesn’t show me everything from big boulders on my path feels sparse. Compare the mapping to what I can get on my Apple Watch from the mapping service in the Outdooractive app (iOS/Android). The Mibro Fit app is somewhat hit-and-miss, but it’s nowhere near as bad as the reviews made it out to be, so I feel it’s improved over the last couple of years. Yes, it’s a bit clunky and rough around the edges, but it did the job. There’s no point bothering with an outdoor smartwatch if the data you’re gathering is inaccurate or incomplete. When reviewing outdoor gadgets, conscious of — and clear about — the fact that I’m one person, and the best I can do is compare one device against another. So, when I was testing the accuracy of the heart rate, SpO2, and location data, I compared them to the Apple Watch Ultra 4. I tested the sensors while resting, walking, and hiking, and compared the data between the two devices. Two conclusions came from my testing: This is an obvious question that a lot of people are going to be asking, but it comes down to this: the Apple Watch is the clear winner, with one big, glaring caveat. From the apps to advanced health features, optional 5G, and built-in payment handling, not to mention safety features such as fall and crash detection, the Apple Watch is better… if you have an iPhone. Also: I tested the world’s first solar AMOLED sports watch – how charging works If you have an Android, the GS Explorer S is the better smartwatch. Compare this to, say, the Apple Watch SE 3, and you get better battery life (18 hours of normal use vs. 20 days), better GPS (single-band vs. dual-band), and better water resistance (164 feet vs. 328 feet, and the GS Explorer S is OK with diving to 98 feet). And if we’re comparing the titanium model, there’s mapping (although there are also plenty of mapping apps for the Apple Watch). It leaves the SE 3 in the dust. I could compare it to the Ultra 4 and say you get a lot of outdoor smartwatch for a lot less, but it’s hard to make a fair comparison either way, given the big price difference and how mature the Apple Watch ecosystem is. If you’re an Android user, the Apple Watch ecosystem isn’t on your radar, so the field is more open since flagships like the Pixel Watch 5 or Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 lean more toward being smartwatches than rugged outdoor watches (the exception being the Galaxy Watch Ultra). Wearables have to fit into people’s style and aesthetic, and what I like might not suit you, so I like to offer some options. Here are a few alternatives you might want to check out: Watches are tough to review because they are so personal. I like big watches, but you might like small ones. I like a lot of information on the display, while you might like the bare minimum. We’re all different. What I can say about the Mibro GS Explorer S is that, for the price (which at the time of writing is $140 and $230 for the ceramic or titanium models, respectively), it’s a very good outdoor smartwatch. Also: Flipper Zero vs. Flipper One: Why the new model isn’t an upgrade If this does interest you, give thought to whether you want the ceramic or titanium version. The key difference is mapping, but I’m not fully sold on it because the map tiles are somewhat small and the routing features are limited when you’re actually on a route. Knowing this might tip you toward the ceramic model, unless you like the titanium look. If you’re a fitness enthusiast, the GS Explorer S will give you all the stats you need to keep you on track, and more, for a very good price, and a device that should give you a good few years of service. title: GS Engineering wins 1.8 trillion won Mokdong reconstruction contract - Chosunbiz
content: GS Engineering & Construction has won the contract to rebuild Mokdong Complex 12 in Seoul's Yangcheon district, a project with construction costs approaching 1.8 trillion won. "Drawing on our distinctive design and experience in urban renewal projects, we will make Replige Xi a residential complex that represents Mokdong," a GS Engineering & Construction representative said. title: GS25 lands in Cambodia with 500-store goal - The Korea Herald
content:
Business GS25 lands in Cambodia with 500-store goal GS25 has opened its first store in Cambodia and aims to operate more than 500 outlets there within 10 years. Cambodia is the South Korean convenience store chain’s third overseas market, following Vietnam and Mongolia. GS Retail, which operates GS25, said Monday it had signed a nationwide master franchise agreement with Cambodian retailer Meta Retail after more than a year of local due diligence and feasibility reviews. The two companies opened the first store, the Olympic Stadium branch, in Phnom Penh on Friday. The roughly 400-square-meter outlet carries about 3,000 products, including items from GS25’s private-label brands Youus and Real Price. Korean-style products, including fish-shaped pastries, snacks, ready-to-eat meals and triangular gimbap, account for about half of the store’s food offerings. The outlet also features a cafe-style area designed to appeal to younger shoppers. Jung Chun-ho, head of GS Retail’s convenience store business unit, attended the opening ceremony alongside Meta Group Chairman Sok Bun Cheng and Meta Retail CEO Heng Sengly. “We will build on our overseas business experience in Vietnam and Mongolia and our Korean-style convenience store operating capabilities to establish a strong foothold in Cambodia,” Jung said. “Through close cooperation with our local partner, we will offer differentiated products and services and continue to strengthen our global competitiveness.” GS25 sees room for growth in Cambodia, where the population is young and convenience stores and minimarts are gaining traction. Meta Retail brings experience in supply chain management, marketing, store operations, recruitment and training. The two companies also plan to draw on the experience of Meta Retail’s parent company, Meta Group, as they expand in Cambodia. GS25 entered Vietnam in 2018 and Mongolia in 2021. As of the end of October, the chain had 740 overseas stores, with 456 in Vietnam and 284 in Mongolia. title: GS E&C Wins 1.8 Trillion Won Mokdong Redevelopment Deal - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
First 'Xi' Brand Project in Mokdong New Town
Complex to Be Reduced to 19 Buildings With Large Central Forest
More Orders Expected in Yeouido and Gwangmyeong GS E&C (006360) has been selected as the contractor for the reconstruction of the Mokdong 12 apartment complex in Seoul's Yangcheon district. With the roughly 1.8 trillion won project in hand, the builder's cumulative urban redevelopment orders this year have passed 7.3 trillion won. If it also secures large projects in Yeouido and Gwangmyeong, where contractors will be chosen late this year, its annual orders are expected to exceed 10 trillion won and reach around 11 trillion won. The Mokdong 12 reconstruction association picked GS E&C as its contractor at a general meeting held the previous day at Dongyang Mirae University in Seoul's Guro district, according to redevelopment industry sources on the 23rd. It marks the first time the company's "Xi" brand will be used in the reconstruction of Mokdong New Town, which comprises 14 complexes. The project will replace 1,860 existing apartment units at 326 Sinjeong-dong in Yangcheon district with 2,810 units across 19 buildings rising up to 41 stories, along with support and welfare facilities. Construction costs total about 1.7887 trillion won. Mokdong 12 sits near Yangcheon-gu Office Station on Seoul's subway Line 2 as well as Sintree Park and Gyenam Park, giving it both transit access and green space. GS E&C proposed "Ripplize Xi" as the complex name, combining "ripple," "luz" for light and the suffix "-ize" to evoke the beautiful transformation of light and water. Under the concept of "building a forest in Mokdong," the builder cut the number of residential buildings to 19 from the 22 in the original plan and created a large central woodland. The complex is planned with 15 themed gardens and about 3 kilometers of walking paths. It will also adopt Clima, a future-oriented climate response system. Sensor-driven flood barriers that detect weather conditions in real time and operate automatically, along with modular rainwater retention tanks, are designed to respond preemptively to extreme weather such as torrential rain, strengthening the complex's safety and the sustainability of its living environment. An "all-in-one high-end community" will offer 60 programs spanning education, exercise, relaxation and dining. Facilities include the Scala Library, all-day dining and an indoor swimming pool, as well as a 110-meter "Scala Bridge" linking three buildings and a sky lounge. GS E&C has won 5.5477 trillion won worth of redevelopment work this year, including the first district of the Seongsu strategic redevelopment zone in Seongdong district, one of the year's biggest prizes at 2.154 trillion won, and the Songpa Hanyang 2 reconstruction in Songpa district at 685.6 billion won. Adding Mokdong 12 brings the cumulative total to 7.3364 trillion won. More orders are lined up for the end of the year. GS E&C has been named preferred bidder for the reconstruction of the Eunha and Samik apartments in Yeouido, Yeongdeungpo district, worth 1.067 trillion won in construction costs, and the Haan Jugong 12 reconstruction in Gwangmyeong, Gyeonggi Province, worth 1.2622 trillion won. title: Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs Walkthrough - IGN
content:
Randy calls Lucia and Jason and asks them to steal a Granforma Zorrusso. This Grand Theft Auto VI Chapter 3 mission is a tutorial for a pivotal tool: the Key Cloner, and this official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through it. This mission can be completed solo or as a pair. It’s a quick one – or at least it should be! Once you arrive at the apartment parking lot, you’ll call Randy for more information. He’ll have one of his guys send you an app for the Key Cloner. Download it, then you’re good to start hunting for the Granforma. You’ll find the red Granforma Zorrusso tucked away in the shadows on the east side of the garage. If you WAiNK It, you’ll see it sells for a whopping $23,375 and has an advanced tracker. Use the Key Cloner to get into the car. Unlocking cars with digital keys is similar to using the Slim Jim to unlock cars with physical keys. Use the right thumbstick to move around the circle until you find the weak spot, indicated by how fast the key clones and the audio cue. Hold it there and the door unlocks, allowing you to enter and drive immediately – no hotwiring required. As Randy said on the call, the only good way to deal with an advanced tracker is to drive fast. You’ll have a very brief grace period after starting the car before the advanced tracker activates. The tracker icon above the minimap begins pulsing and the circle around it fills with red as the tracker activates. Once the ring is completely filled red, the local police are notified about the car’s theft, earning you an instant two-star Wanted level. The only way to prevent activating the tracker is by moving fast, constantly. If you speed up enough as the tracker ring fills, you can cancel the alarm.
Do your best to get out of the area as fast and as safely as possible. Any damage you do to the car now reduces the payout you’ll get for delivering it in perfect condition. One of the best ways to get to Randy with the space to drive fast is by taking the highway. Drive just fast enough so the tracker isn’t getting set off, but not so fast that you can’t control the car. If you set off the advanced tracker of any car, the police respond to the location where it was set off, not where you are exactly as you drive – unless a cop spotted you as the tracker went off. Then they'll pursue you and you'll need to shake them like you would normally. As setting off a tracker only warrants a two-star Wanted level, passing into another district, county, or region puts you and the car in the clear so long as you're not being actively chased by cops. Be sure to keep moving fast, though, because the tracker can go off again if you drive too slow. Advanced tracker signals are blocked near Randy’s showroom, so I’d recommend slowing the cars as you get off the highway to avoid crashing at the last second. Pull into Randy’s garage to deliver the car and get your payment. After taking a look at the car, Randy asks you to join him over at a big whiteboard with “WANTED” written on top. He introduces a list of 15 cars a client of his wants. If you can find and bring the listed cars to Randy in top condition, you can make a lot of money.
Now when you scan cars out in Leonida, you'll get an extra notification if you find a car on Randy’s list. You can see the car list any time in the Robberies menu of the Map, under Randy’s Wish List. We also have a guide with hints on where to find each of the cars. You can talk to Randy more if you’d like, but leave when you’re ready. If you need a car, you can use one of the three branded cars for free just outside the showroom. As you leave, Randy texts you if you earned a condition bonus payment for the car you delivered. If you delivered the Granforma in perfect condition, you’ll get an extra $10,000. With this mission complete, you can now work on a new optional mission called Randy's Wish List. Check IGN's official guide page for help with these vehicles. Now that you have the Key Cloner, practically no civilian car is off limits. If you’re ready to continue with missions, you may have one of these ready to go next: This walkthrough features some first-person elements. Those come from IGN's GTA 6 Lead Editor, Miranda Sanchez. You can learn more about Miranda and her experience on the About the GTA 6 Guide Editors page.

title: Seawolves sweep opening races of Alaska Nordic Cup - Seawolf Athletics
content:

11/21/2026 8:53:00 PM
Ian Marks - Assistant Athletic Director - Media Relations FAIRBANKS, ALASKA – Marlie Molinaro and Erling Bjornstad swept the individual titles for Alaska Anchorage in the 15-kilometer freestyle races on the first day of the Alaska Cup in Fairbanks. The Seawolves lead their rivals the Nanooks by 1:04 heading into the freestyle sprint relay Sunday. Marlie Molinaro won the women's race in 43:19. Constance LaPointe finished third (43:31), and Hedda Halvari was fourth (43:41). Aria Grandi was ninth (45:04), and Dashe McCabe was 13th (46:28). Corbin Carpenter was sixth (35:47), Parke Chapin seventh (36:40) and Hermod Bangstad eighth (36:41). Henry Skjoensfjel placed 11th (37:26), Chase Laker 14th (37:34) and Garrett Siever 15th (37:51). "The first race of the season is a chance to see where we are at and how the skiers have responded to training," said associate head coach Trond Flagstad. "We are happy to see that we are on the right track with two wins and a solid team effort that puts us in the lead after Day one. Tomorrow is a new race and new opportunities to work on race strategies. We are excited about the relay format and the chance to go head-to-head with UAF to try to bring the Alaska Nordic Cup back to Anchorage." Copyright © 2026. University of Alaska Anchorage Athletics.
